bootstrap.unit: 12 base tasks; operations and nested budgets remain within each task

analysis.coverage: A new seed on known development tasks; no independent-task or sealed-holdout validation
analysis.curves: Report all six history-operation success curves at budgets1/2/3, fixed candidate bounds, signed distance from the candidate interval, and task-bootstrap95 intervals for empirical values
analysis.decision: Diagnose predictive departures; no automatic gate, parameter refit, or theorem rejection from candidate bounds. A bounds cover semantic assignment only, not parameter or state error.
analysis.failure_labels: Codex full-text E/C/U/A review with prior hashes reused. Starting visible E => restatement; definite absence with no A => generation; A-only uncertainty remains unresolved.
analysis.interpretation: Check initial E+C conflict and C versus empty first; later departures also involve native wording, failure-selected task composition, state compression, and sampling uncertainty.
analysis.native_update: Run complete author attempts and append exactly one reflection after each failure, including terminal failure. Later attempts consume the full growing history through the author last-three visibility rule.
analysis.old_error_tracking: Track initial entries by origin index after the one recovery; corrected E is no longer an old error, deleted E has no origin, new reflections are new entries even if their text repeats.
analysis.primary: For repeated_error at budget two, report task-paired correct_latest minus delete_latest success difference with task-bootstrap95 interval against the existing conditional candidate gain bounds

entries.C: Plan: Before I heat an object with the microwave, I must keep it in my inventory. I should continue working on the household task.
entries.E: Plan: Before I heat an object with the microwave, I must put it inside the microwave. I should continue working on the household task.
entries.N: Plan: I should continue working on the household task.

scientific_questions: Do initial correction and deletion share a success curve for a single E, as the presence-only candidate predicts?
For E,N,E, does correcting versus deleting the latest E produce the predicted budget-two difference when the older E exits at different updates?
Do forecast departures begin at the first attempt or after native reflection updates, and which task paths accompany them?
scope: Known-task multiround process diagnosis with one initial recovery and native later updates
